title: Transolver: A Fast Transformer Solver for PDEs on General Geometries
layout_note: Left third: a standard pre-norm block, dashed zoom lines from its attention box into a small block diagram of that attention; a vertical dashed rule; right two-thirds: the same attention drawn again with the data — an input field slab fanned into a staircase of weighted field slabs, pooled into token cubes, mixed, broadcast back and merged into an output field slab.
grouping: The layer is a dashed rounded container read bottom-to-top; its zoom is a solid black rounded panel with stacked offset frames behind for the heads. The right half has no container; a two-entry legend at its top-left explains the token cube and the green arrow. Colour families: pale green for LayerNorm, pale blue for feed-forward and the slice/deslice boxes, pale pink for the proposed attention; dark-red text for the token-attention step in both the block diagram and the data drawing; brown curved arrows for slice weights; navy lines for slicing and de-slicing; green arrows for aggregate and broadcast.
shapes_depth: Left: flat rounded rectangles with thin outlines and bold sans labels, circled-plus residual nodes. Right: 3-D slabs (thick plates seen in perspective) whose front faces carry the field on the mesh as colormapped contours (purple for input and output, yellow-green for the weighted slices, blue gradients for broadcast copies); tokens are small shaded 3-D cubes in blue tints joined by a web of thin pale-red lines. Tensor sizes (N x C, M x C, M x (N x C)) sit in sans text under the slabs and cubes; step names (Slice, DeSlice, Slice Weights) are bold italic on the canvas.
proposed_highlight: The proposed attention is the only pink box in the standard block and is expanded twice, first as a block diagram, then as a data drawing; the token-attention step is in dark-red text in both, which ties the two expansions together.
lesson: Explain the new operator twice side by side — a small block diagram zoomed from its box, then the same steps drawn on the physical field itself (field slab split into weighted copies, pooled into a few token cubes, broadcast back) — and give the shared step the same text colour in both.
notes: Venue from the PDF footer ('Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning'; venue_source: pdf). The field faces are embedded images recorded by refs crop and left out of the palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: the large right panel performs Physics-Attention on a drawn field: an N x C mesh slab is 'Slice'd by fanning blue lines into a staircase of M weighted copies of the field, each aggregated by a green arrow into one physics-aware token cube, the tokens attend to each other through a pink web of edges, are broadcast back to M slabs, and 'DeSlice' blue lines converge into the output N x C slab

relations.form: the field is drawn as a coloured mesh image around an airfoil-like hole, repeated on each slice slab with different weight colourings, so slicing is shown on the data
left to right: input slab -> Slice -> M slice slabs (M x (N x C)) -> M tokens (M x C) -> attention -> M tokens -> M broadcast slabs -> DeSlice -> output slab, each stage labelled with its shape below
a brown arc labelled 'Slice Weights N x M' sweeps over the top from Slice to DeSlice, the same weights used to split and to recombine

on the left a transformer block (LayerNorm, Physics-Attention, LayerNorm, Feed-Forward with residual pluses) has its pink Physics-Attention box opened by two dashed lines into a panel: Linear -> Slice -> Aggregate -> Attention for Tokens -> Broadcast -> Deslice -> Linear, with a Slice Weights slab beside it and stacked frames labelled 'Heads'
at DeSlice, blue lines from every broadcast slab converge on one point before the output slab

channels.colour: blue lines and blue labels = slice/deslice assignment, green arrows = aggregate and broadcast (keyed), brown = slice weights (arc, label and detail-panel slab), pink/red = attention among tokens (edge web, 'Attention for Tokens' label, the Physics-Attention block fill), navy shades = token cubes; the same codes hold between the detail panel and the big panel; field colours inside slabs = physical values; blue also fills the unrelated Feed-Forward block
channels.shape: slabs in perspective = fields over the mesh; small cubes = physics-aware tokens; rounded rectangles = layers
channels.line: solid coloured lines = the operations named above; dashed black lines = zoom tie; a vertical dashed line separates the two panels
channels.frame: a dashed rounded frame = one transformer block; a solid rounded panel = the Physics-Attention module with stacked copies for heads

quality.strengths: the new attention is the largest element and is drawn on the structure it acts on - the reader sees N mesh points fold into M slice tokens and unfold again, with tensor shapes under every stage; the detail panel and the big panel use the same words and colours (Slice, Aggregate, Broadcast, Deslice, brown Slice Weights), so the module and its picture can be matched term by term; the shared slice weights are one arc spanning exactly from Slice to DeSlice
quality.weaknesses: the pink all-to-all attention web and the fanning blue slice lines overlap the token row, making the middle of the panel busy; the staircase of perspective slabs partly hides each slice's field; blue fills the Feed-Forward block while also meaning slice assignment

insights.structure: Left third: a dashed pre-norm layer with a zoom into a black-framed block diagram of Physics-Attention (stacked frames for heads); a vertical dashed rule; right two-thirds: the same attention drawn again with the data.
insights.data: The input field is a 3-D slab with a flow-field texture, fanned by navy lines into a staircase of slabs weighted by slice weights, pooled into small blue token cubes, mixed by pink attention lines, then broadcast back to blue-gradient slabs and merged into an output slab; shapes labelled N x C, M x (N x C), M x C.
insights.emphasis: Physics-Attention is the only pink box in the layer and its token step is dark-red text in both the block diagram and the data drawing, tying the two views together.
insights.flow: The left layer reads bottom to top; the right half reads left to right Slice -> Attention for Tokens -> DeSlice, with a brown arc for slice weights over the top.
insights.avoid: The right half's many crossing navy and pink lines make individual slices hard to trace; a lighter or fewer-slice version would read faster.

arrangement.units: left: dashed layer box plus a solid zoom panel; right (after a dashed vertical rule): unframed data drawing of the same module
arrangement.inputs_as: a textured 3-D slab of the physical field
